keep: The idea is named in one line up front: a grid read across as equations and down as arrows, and grid times a column of amounts mixes the columns.

The picture is the brief's Mix two arrows: two column arrows, sliders for x and y, the mix nose to tail as in Vectors lesson 3, rows and columns lit on tap, dragged tips, and a target dot that is a pair of simultaneous equations.

One worked example computed from the rule: [1 3; 2 1] times (2, 1) is 2 lots of (1, 2) plus (3, 1), landing on (5, 5), checked by both rows. The target (7, 4) is x + 3y = 7 and 2x + y = 4, giving x = 1 and y = 2.
The main grid is not the same either side of its diagonal, so rows read as arrows give a different point, (4, 7). The rows-against-columns slip can be seen failing.

Twelve screens alternate SHOW (1, 3, 5, 7, 9) and DO (2, 4, 6, 8, 10), ending with two mixed puzzles (11, 12). Each lesson 1 mistake in the brief has a puzzle: rows against columns (2, 4, 11), procedure without picture (6, predicted before the chain is drawn), x read one way only (8).
Three footnotes, each on a rule he might look up. No source is named in the text.
fix: Causal step skipped: 'row 1 adds the across parts' is asserted. Say why: the top number of each column is that arrow's across part, so row 1 holds every arrow's across part.
Causal step skipped: the rows-as-arrows slip is shown failing but not explained. Say a row is not an arrow: it holds one part of each arrow.
False absolute: 'Across, each row holds the numbers of one equation' is said of every matrix. Qualify it: when a grid holds a set of equations.

Notation used before it is explained: [4 7 1; 2 5 3] appears in explain and practice with no word on the semicolons. Say once that a grid on one line is written row by row with a semicolon between rows.
Vague course-puzzle sentence: 'the amounts that hit a target'. Say the target is the column of loop voltages.

ignores: 'The grids are 2 by 2' is false for screen 1's 2 by 3 grid, and 'cannot be drawn flat' is loose. Say the arrows come from 2 by 2 grids, three parts need a 3-D drawing and more cannot be drawn.

whatAmILookingAt: puzzles 11 and 12 are named but not set. Give their numbers and choices so the builder invents nothing, say the chain is drawn only after Check on the predicting puzzles, and say the three answers wrap on a phone.
No other false absolutes: 'two arrows along one line can only reach points on that line' holds for any amounts, and 'every x multiplies a number from column 1' holds for any 2 by 2 grid.
